title: Does my game have a chance on mobile or will people dismiss it?
author: ukjadoon
selftext: This has been an ongoing project for almost 7-8 years with me trying to fund it multiple times with freelancers/artists but it was just impossible to finish or the artwork was just not where I wanted it (or I always ran out of money). This year I revived the project and have been working relentlessly (with a lot of AI help) and am close to finishing it. I really hope that people enjoy the game for what it is and not just hate on it for using AI because only I know how many times I have revived/killed the project in the last decade and without AI I probably would never have been able to finish it. I am really scared of launching it, please give me some hope and feedback. Thanks!

comments.author: PositiveScarcity8909
comments.body: Could have been a hit if you had released it 20 years earlier.

comments.author: Happy_Guitar3521
comments.body:
I like it, but doubt in any success. Most of the earnings on mobile are coming not from heart and passion of developer, but from psychology of addicting patterns in app where companies are paying more than 500 grands a month for ads. 

My suggestion (I am developer but not a gamedev) is that if you are building something with passion you should create community around the game and the game development progress. 

Also the last pessimistic thing is that reallity looks now that if you got a good idea, there will be company that would copy your game in one week with much better budget. 

I can be wrong of course.

replies.author: ukjadoon
replies.body: u/Happy_Guitar3521 thank you for your honest feedback. I never planned the game around some kind of an addictive pay to win loop but I do hope people who like old school barrier defence games still dig it. I hope that people also enjoy the electronic, industrial/thrash metal soundtrack and the totally bonkers story. Being such an introvert, it is hard to work on building a community but I will try to promote, talk about it on Twitter and ask some streamers to try it. I will try to be cautiously optimistic and see where it goes but I am not hoping for much.

replies.author: Happy_Guitar3521
replies.body: Yes, definetely try Twitter, different Reddit boards and maybe Tiktok. You need to find your audience. There will definetely be people interested in, but the volume can be not that big.

replies.author: ukjadoon
replies.body: Thanks, yeah, didn't think about Tiktok. I should probably do that closer the game's release perhaps so that people can at least download/try it out immediately when they see it.

replies.author: Happy_Guitar3521
replies.body:
Try to think about it. Building community takes time, if you got playable enjoyable game in early access it should be good enough to start with the community, maybe even earlier. You just have to try and do not be affraid, even if you won't have any success you will gain knowledge how to make it better in another project. Every experience, and mostly those bad can teach you something. 

I was there many times (not as a game dev).

replies.author: ukjadoon
replies.body: Yes, I agree. It is a challenge to release the game in early access on Android I believe since the Play Store doesn't allow early access users to leave reviews which would be pretty bad to gather valuable feedback but I'll see if there are some other options, otherwise the main launch shouldn't be farther than 1-2 months from now. i am quite close to finishing anyway, just polishing things here and there at the moment.

comments.author: XalAtoh
comments.body:
300 games released yesterday, none of them were succesful.

Today another 300 games have released, none of them were succesful.

What makes you think your game will be succesful?

Trying to give you hope, is just evil.

replies.author: anon999387
replies.body: And 175,000 people die each day...gotta shoot your shot

replies.author: ukjadoon
replies.body: Sure, even if I fail, its not going to be the end of the world, but at least I tried and learned something along the way and I think I'll die on this hill.

replies.author: derAres
replies.body: This indeed appears to be the way.

comments.author: DoctaRoboto
comments.body: I think you have little chance of success, not just because of AI, but also because a Plants Vs Zombies clone at this age is a bit too late to the party.

comments.author: Ryedarn
comments.body: Forget Mobile, Put it on Steam/Browser and I'll check it out.
